report.source_text: He was advised to undergo a nephrostomy for ureteral dilation followed by double J stent placement. A percutaneous approach for cyst removal was deemed very difficult in this patient, thus nephrostomy was conducted using an 8-8.9 Fr nephroscope. To be able to remove the cyst, the cyst wall had to be very thin and well-visualized to avoid renal parenchyma injury. However, in our case, the cyst wall was too thick and poorly visualized, thus cyst removal was not conducted. Cyst removal failed, thus we proceeded to perform ureteral dilatation. The double J stent was inserted and bleeding was checked. Four months after surgery, the cyst remained, but the patient was asymptomatic.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Posterior Peritoneal Cyst (PPC) causing hydronephrosis and pelvico-ureteric junction obstruction (PUJO)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 27-year-old male presented with a 3-year history of partial urinary retention and intermittent loin pain. Initial clinical evaluation revealed normal vital signs, physical examination, hematology, renal function, and urinalysis. Ultrasound identified pelvicalyceal dilatation and proximal ureteral dilation consistent with PUJO, but could not identify the source of obstruction. CT imaging revealed a 5.03 × 5.36 × 5.98 cm hypodense lesion in the renal pelvis extending to the proximal ureter, not filled with contrast. The cyst was compressing the right renal pelvic system and proximal ureter, causing PUJO with grade III hydronephrosis. The patient underwent nephroscopy with attempted cyst removal, but the cyst wall was found to be too thick and poorly visualized, precluding safe removal. Instead, ureteral dilation and double J stent placement were performed. Four months postoperatively, the cyst remained in place but the patient was asymptomatic.
